answer: To resist sybil attacks in an agent economy, agents must complete a costly proof-of-identity voyage that ties each identity to a unique physical or computational anchor, such as a willow-tree-like branching verification tree rooted in real-world sensors or stake. An attacker forging many identities would face prohibitive costs replicating these anchors across a shifting dune of network challenges, making mass duplication economically irrational while legitimate agents voyage once to establish trust.
